rationale: Observations: baseline 128x64x64 s1 t256 sw0 = 3560.55us. 32x256x32 s1 t256 sw64 = 3518.99us (DRAM 451MB). 32x256x32 s1 t128 sw64 = 2504.88us (best, 330MB, 3 blocks/SM). Attempt-04 64x128x32 s2 t256 sw64 = 3989.52us, so stage=2 with narrower N and t256 regressed. Key lessons: threads=128 beats 256 at equal tile/stage/swizzle (more blocks/SM), swizzle>=64 with narrow M/wide N lowers DRAM, and stage=1 wide-N is competitive while s2 regressed. This plan fixes previous schema issues by returning full required JSON with nonempty domains. I keep block_N=256 and swizzle>=8 to test whether panel locality gains persist, drop swizzle=0 to force exploration away from row-major (already tested), and narrow threads to {128,64} since 128 previously won and 256 regressed at s2. Stages remain [1,2,3,4] to test both s1 retention and whether deeper pipelines recover. Weights: traffic raised to 2 (DRAM reduction correlated with latency), launches lowered to 0.5 (grid already large), pipeline at 1 since stage benefit is unproven. The estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages,4*block_M*block_N) with hard 32768 cap prunes oversized combos. Scope: Metal checks simulate exact source/config/TIR; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 numbers are simulator estimates, not hardware. Next hypothesis: confirm t128 wins with a different tile (e.g. block_N=256, block_M=32/64) and test whether block_K=64/128 at stage>=2 beats the s1 wide-N best; if simulator traffic gains from swizzle do not translate to latency, reduce traffic weight next round.
